entry.name: Avebury
entry.description: Great standing stones encircle a grassy hollow. Raised in Britain long before written records, this vast monument holds smaller circles within it. What ceremonies once drew people here?

entry.name: Pompey's Pillar
entry.description: In Alexandria, a towering red granite column rises above the broken remains of an ancient temple. Raised in honor of a Roman emperor, it is now known to sailors by Pompey's name.

entry.name: Step Pyramid of Djoser
entry.description: In the desert south of Cairo rises a great stone tomb of six rising tiers. Built for King Djoser, the pyramid stands among courtyards and shrines, a marvel of Egypt's oldest royal builders.

entry.name: Nile Perch
entry.description: In the upper Nile swims a giant fish with silver scales and a ravenous mouth. It waits in deep river channels, then strikes at smaller fish with startling speed.

entry.name: Meroe Pyramids
entry.description: Sharp pyramids rise from the Nubian sands beside the old kingdom of Kush. Though smaller than Egypt's, these royal tombs stand in long rows beneath the desert sun.

entry.name: Danakil Depression
entry.description: A harsh land of salt, steam, and burning color spreads across the desert floor. Strange pools and smoking vents make this one of the most otherworldly sights in Africa.

entry.name: Frankincense Tree
entry.description: From the stony slopes of the Horn rises a crooked tree whose bark yields fragrant tears of resin. Caravans prize this incense, carrying its scent to distant shrines and markets.

entry.name: African Rock Python
entry.description: Near the lakes and rivers of eastern Africa coils a mighty patterned serpent. Hidden among reeds and rocks, it waits for prey before closing its powerful body around it.

entry.name: Lake Tanganyika
entry.description: Between the steep ridges of the African Rift stretches a vast blue lake. Its waters run for hundreds of miles between rocky shores and shelter a world of strange fish.

entry.name: Benin Earthworks
entry.description: Great banks of red earth and deep moats surround the ancient kingdom of Benin. These mighty walls run past forest and village, guarding the roads to the royal city.

entry.name: Bandiagara Cliffs
entry.description: Towering sandstone cliffs break the dry plains of Mali. Villages cling to their ledges, with small houses and granaries sheltered beneath walls of glowing red rock.

entry.name: Sankore Mosque
entry.description: Beyond the sandy streets of Timbuktu stands a mosque built of earth and timber. Travelers gather here to pray and study, while scholars discuss books carried across the desert.

entry.name: Giant Pangolin
entry.description: In the forested country by the great Congo rivers walks a giant creature clad in overlapping scales. Its long claws tear into termite mounds, while a sticky tongue gathers the insects within.

entry.name: Goliath Tigerfish
entry.description: Deep in the Congo's powerful rivers swims a silver hunter armed with long, daggerlike teeth. It strikes smaller fish amid the current, and even skilled boatmen keep their hands clear of its jaws.

entry.name: Kasai River
entry.description: Across the heart of central Africa flows a great brown river, gathering many streams beneath the rainforest. Broad channels wind among green banks on their way to the Congo.

entry.name: Hartmann's Zebra
entry.description: Upon the dry mountain slopes of southwestern Africa roams a striped wild horse. Its narrow hoofprints cross rocky gullies as it searches for grass and precious water.

entry.name: Cederberg Rock Art
entry.description: In sheltered caves north of the Cape, red and ochre figures of eland and hunters cover the stone. These ancient paintings preserve traces of the San people's sacred traditions.

entry.name: Blombos Cave
entry.description: On the southern African coast a sheltered cavern holds traces of people from ages long past. Shells, stone tools, and red ochre reveal the work of skilled ancient hands.

entry.name: Dugong
entry.description: Off the eastern African shore a gentle sea grazer rises to breathe, then sinks among the seagrass beds. Its broad muzzle and heavy, fluked body have inspired many a sailor's tale.

entry.name: Aye-Aye
entry.description: On Madagascar lives a strange night creature with huge ears, bright eyes, and a thin tapping finger. It creeps through the forest after dark in search of grubs hidden in wood.

entry.name: Humpback Whale
entry.description: In the warm waters east of Madagascar, an immense whale rises in a spray of foam. Long white-edged flippers cut the sea as it rolls, then its dark body vanishes below the waves.

entry.name: Doum Palm
entry.description: Beside the Nile and dry wadis grows a palm with forked trunks and fanlike leaves. Its hard fruits and strong fibers are prized by the peoples of the river lands.

entry.name: Baba Gurgur Flame
entry.description: From stony ground beyond the gulf, a flame bursts where gases seep from the earth. Travelers have long marveled at this fire, which can burn without any wood to feed it.

entry.name: Dholavira
entry.description: Stone reservoirs, gates, and ordered streets fill this ancient city of the western Indus world. Its builders mastered water and trade in a dry land ringed by salt flats.

entry.name: Indian Peafowl
entry.description: This splendid bird walks the dry plains in gleaming blue and green. When it opens its great tail, a hundred jeweled eyes seem to shimmer in the sun.

entry.name: Mergui Archipelago
entry.description: West of the Malay Peninsula lies a maze of green islands amid clear blue waters. Forests hide deep coves and quiet beaches, while coral gardens flourish beneath the waves.

entry.name: Sukhothai Ruins
entry.description: Broken walls, lotus ponds, and serene Buddha images remain from an early Siamese capital. Quiet temples and towers still rise above the plain.

entry.name: Sumatran Orangutan
entry.description: High in the rain forest swings a great red ape with long arms and thoughtful eyes. It moves from branch to branch slowly, feeding on fruit in the humid canopy.

entry.name: Banteay Srei
entry.description: Deep among the Khmer temples stands a shrine of red sandstone, its doorways covered in fine carvings. Every lintel bears figures and curling vines cut with astonishing skill.

entry.name: Saola
entry.description: In the shadowed forests of the Annamite mountains lives a rare horned beast scarcely seen by men. Its long straight horns and pale face mark it as a wonder of the wild.

entry.name: Ginkgo Tree
entry.description: This ancient tree bears fan-shaped leaves unlike those of any other broadleaf. In autumn its crown turns gold, and its kind is said to descend from a far older world.

entry.name: Sannai-Maruyama Ruins
entry.description: In northern Japan lie the traces of a vast ancient village. Great timber posts, earth pits, and old hearths mark a settlement whose people lived here long before the age of samurai.

entry.name: Clay Dogu
entry.description: A tiny clay figure with wide eyes and strange patterned limbs rests in the northern hills of Japan. Its ancient maker left no explanation; some believe such images served a role in healing rites.

entry.name: Longmen Grottoes
entry.description: Along the cliffs by a river, countless sacred figures have been carved into stone. Serene Buddhas sit within deep niches, their faces watching the waters flow far below.

entry.name: Xanadu Ruins
entry.description: On the windswept grasslands north of China lie the walls of Xanadu, once a seat of Kublai Khan. Earth banks still trace the palaces and streets where Mongol and Chinese traditions met.

entry.name: Pallas's Cat
entry.description: A small, thick-furred wildcat hides among stones on the cold northern steppes of China. Its flat face and rounded ears make it look fierce, though it seldom shows itself.

entry.name: Golden Snub-Nosed Monkey
entry.description: Among the high forests of central China climbs a monkey with golden fur and a striking blue face. Its thick coat guards against cold mountain air, and its troop calls from the treetops.

entry.name: American Black Bear
entry.description: In the broad forests of eastern North America wanders a powerful black-furred bear. It turns stones for insects and feeds on berries and nuts before the cold of winter.

entry.name: Etowah Mounds
entry.description: Beside a river rise tall earthen mounds built by the people of the southeastern lands. Broad plazas and high platforms reveal a great center of ceremony, farming, and trade.

entry.name: Olmec Jade Celt
entry.description: A polished green celt of sacred stone was shaped by ancient hands and treasured in ceremony. Its smooth surface and rich color made jade a symbol of power and life.

entry.name: Bacalar Lagoon
entry.description: Near the southern Yucatan coast lies a long freshwater lagoon, where shallow shelves shine turquoise and deeper waters turn blue. Green forest and marshes fringe its quiet shores.

entry.name: Divi-Divi Tree
entry.description: On the dry Caribbean shore grows a crooked tree, bent as though forever bowing to the wind. Its twisted seedpods contain a rich tanning substance prized by those who work with hides.

entry.name: Scarlet Ibis
entry.description: Bright red birds gather in the mangrove shallows of the southern Caribbean. Their long curved bills probe the mud while flocks glow like embers against the green coast.

entry.name: Prairie Blazing Star
entry.description: Across the open central plains rises a slender wand of rose-purple blossoms above the grass. Its deep roots hold fast through dry seasons, and winged insects crowd its bright flowers.

entry.name: Great Lakes
entry.description: A chain of vast inland seas spreads across the northern forests. Cold blue waters meet rocky shores and pine-clad islands, forming one of the grandest freshwater realms on earth.

entry.name: Kapok Tree
entry.description: A mighty trunk towers above the tropical forest, held upright by enormous roots like wooden walls. High in its crown hang pods filled with a soft, pale fiber.

entry.name: Electric Eel
entry.description: In muddy tropical waters glides a long fish able to unleash a numbing shock. Fishermen fear its hidden strength where roots and reeds darken the river.

entry.name: Amazon Flood Forest
entry.description: When the great Amazon rises, river water sweeps between trees until the forest becomes a maze of channels. Canoes pass among trunks while fish swim where roots once stood dry.

entry.name: Hoatzin
entry.description: Above the flooded forests of northern South America perches a curious bird with a ragged crest. It feeds on leaves and gives off a strong odor, earning a strange reputation among boatmen.

entry.name: Muisca Tunjo
entry.description: A small gold figure stands with rigid limbs and a solemn face. Such offerings were shaped by the Muisca and placed at sacred sites as gifts to powers beyond the ordinary world.

entry.name: Arapaima
entry.description: Beneath the brown waters of the Amazon moves an immense fish plated in heavy scales. It rises to gulp air before sinking again into the flooded forest channels.

entry.name: Spectacled Bear
entry.description: In the misty forests of the Andes lives a black bear with pale rings around its eyes. It climbs steep slopes and trees to feed on fruit and tender plants.

entry.name: Black Caiman
entry.description: Hidden in the dark channels of the Amazon lies a mighty black caiman. Only its eyes and armored brow break the water as it watches prey from the shadows.

entry.name: Blue-footed Booby
entry.description: A bold seabird rests upon rocks above the Pacific surf. Its feet shine an astonishing blue, and it dives like an arrow into the sea to catch its prey.

entry.name: Greater Rhea
entry.description: Across the grassy plains of southern South America runs a tall, flightless bird. Long legs carry it swiftly through the pampas, while its broad wings spread as it turns to escape danger.

entry.name: Guarani Pottery
entry.description: A finely shaped earthen vessel bears dark bands and painted lines. Such pottery is made by Guarani communities of the southern river lands, to hold food and water in daily life.

entry.name: Glyptodon
entry.description: In the plains of the southern continent old bones tell of an enormous armored beast. Its round shell was plated like a fortress, and its heavy tail bore a fearsome weight.

entry.name: Maned Wolf
entry.description: Across the grasslands of southern South America walks a tall reddish hunter on long black legs. It hunts small creatures and fruit in the open country at dusk.

entry.name: Magellanic Penguin
entry.description: Along cold southern shores stands a black-and-white bird with a pink band at the eye. It comes ashore in great colonies and dives swiftly after fish in the surf.

entry.name: Huemul Deer
entry.description: In the cold mountains of southern Chile roams a sturdy deer with short legs and branching antlers. It keeps to wooded slopes and rocky valleys where few travelers pass.

entry.name: Atacama Desert
entry.description: Between the Pacific and the high Andes stretches a barren realm of stone, salt, and red hills. Whole valleys may wait years for rain beneath a cloudless sky.

entry.name: Sacsayhuaman
entry.description: High above Cuzco stand mighty terraces built from enormous interlocking stones. Their precise joints and commanding height show the skill of the Inca builders.

entry.name: Zenu Gold Pectoral
entry.description: A broad golden pendant gleams with hammered patterns and the forms of river creatures. Metalworkers of the northern lands shaped such treasures for display and ceremony.

entry.name: El Cano Stone Circles
entry.description: Across the river plains of Panama stand weathered stone columns and ancient burial grounds. The people who raised them left carved stones and offerings beneath the tropical earth.

entry.name: Usulutan Vessel
entry.description: An old clay vessel carries winding reddish lines upon a pale body. Potters of the southern Maya region mastered this subtle pattern by keeping parts of the clay free from pigment.

entry.name: Maya Cacao Cup
entry.description: A painted clay vessel bears noble figures and fine ornaments from the old Maya cities. Cups like this held cacao, beaten into a dark froth and shared at feasts and important gatherings.

entry.name: Maya Eccentric Flint
entry.description: A blade of flint has been chipped into a winding shape, with slender points that serve no common tool. Maya craftsmen placed such extraordinary works in sacred offerings.

entry.name: Monte Alban
entry.description: High above a valley in southern Mexico lie great stone terraces and courts. The Zapotec built this hilltop city with temples, tombs and wide plazas beneath the open sky.

entry.name: Las Labradas
entry.description: On a rocky shore in the west of Mexico, strange spirals, beasts, and human shapes have been carved into dark stone. Ocean waves wash across these signs left by ancient hands.

entry.name: Desert Bighorn
entry.description: In the jagged mountains of the western deserts climbs a powerful sheep with curled horns. It leaps among dry ledges where few other creatures can keep their footing.

entry.name: California Condor
entry.description: High above the western mountains circles an immense black bird with bright patches beneath its wings. It sails for hours upon rising air, searching the distant ground below.

entry.name: California Sea Otter
entry.description: Along the cold Pacific shore floats a small furred swimmer, cracking shellfish upon a stone. It rests among kelp beds beyond the surf and dives with nimble paws.

entry.name: Banten Girang Ruins
entry.description: Near Java's western strait lie old banks and stone-cut chambers beside a river. These are traces of Banten Girang, a vanished settlement that once watched the busy waterways of the island.

entry.name: Javan Tiger
entry.description: In the thick forests of Java moves a fierce striped cat, silent and heavy-footed. Hunters fear its sudden leap from the undergrowth, where its orange coat vanishes in shadow.

entry.name: Saltwater Crocodile
entry.description: In the creeks and mangroves of the eastern islands lurks a mighty reptile, armored with rough scales. Only its eyes show above the tide before it strikes without warning.

entry.name: Greater Bilby
entry.description: A shy night-dweller of Australia's dry country has long ears, a pointed snout, and strong digging claws. It leaves winding tracks beside burrows in the red sand.

entry.name: Western Quoll
entry.description: In the woodlands of southwestern Australia prowls a spotted night hunter with a pointed face. It shelters in hollow logs by day, then seeks insects and small prey beneath the stars.

entry.name: Kata Tjuta
entry.description: Beyond the red desert plain rise immense rounded domes of stone, divided by narrow gorges. These hills hold deep meaning for the Anangu people, whose sacred stories are their own to share.

entry.name: Bare-nosed Wombat
entry.description: On the cool wooded island south of Australia lives a stout burrowing grazer. With powerful claws it digs deep shelters and feeds on grass in the evening.

entry.name: Platypus
entry.description: In the clear streams of southeastern Australia swims a curious furred creature with a broad bill and webbed feet. It dives among stones, hunting small animals hidden beneath the water.

entry.name: Palm Cockatoo
entry.description: In the northern forests of Australia a great black cockatoo raises its long crest above a red cheek. Its mighty beak cracks hard nuts, and its deep voice carries through the treetops.

entry.name: Southern Cassowary
entry.description: In the forests of New Guinea stalks a tall, flightless bird with a hornlike crown and a bright blue neck. Its powerful feet bear sharp claws, while fallen fruit makes up much of its food.

entry.name: Leang-Leang Caves
entry.description: Within limestone caves on the island of Sulawesi, red handprints and figures mark ancient stone walls. The painted signs endure in the cool darkness far beyond the memory of their makers.

entry.name: Rafflesia
entry.description: On the jungle floor blooms a giant red flower speckled in pale dots. Its heavy petals open around a deep center, making it one of the most astonishing blossoms in the tropics.

entry.name: Philippine Eagle
entry.description: A towering eagle watches the forest from a high branch, its wild crest raised above a hooked beak. With broad wings it glides between the mountains of these green islands.

entry.name: Nutmeg Tree
entry.description: This spice tree bears pale fruits that split to reveal a dark seed wrapped in crimson lace. From these fragrant kernels come prized seasonings sought across the seas.

entry.name: Tuatara
entry.description: On lonely islets near New Zealand dwells a spiny-backed reptile with the look of ancient days. It hides in burrows and moves quietly among seabird colonies.

entry.name: Atlantic Puffin
entry.description: Upon windy sea cliffs stands a black-and-white bird with a bright beak and orange feet. It nests in burrows near the North Atlantic, returning to land in the summer season.

entry.name: Sun Dogs
entry.description: In the northern sky two bright phantoms sometimes flank the low sun, as if three suns shone at once. These strange lights appear where sunlight bends through tiny ice crystals in the air.

entry.name: Walrus
entry.description: On the icebound northern seas rests a massive, whiskered beast with two ivory tusks. Its sensitive bristles help it seek shellfish beneath the cold, shallow water of the Bering Sea.

entry.name: Narwhal
entry.description: Beneath the drifting ice swims a pale whale with a long spear-like tusk. Mariners of the far north prize tales of this strange beast of the frozen sea.

entry.name: Qalupalik
entry.description: In tales told across the northern ice, a strange being waits in dark water below the frozen shore. People warn travelers to heed the cracking floes and keep clear of treacherous ice.

entry.name: Polar Bear
entry.description: Upon the frozen shores of Greenland prowls a huge white bear, its broad paws spreading over snow and ice. It hunts seals at the edge of the sea, disappearing against the pale horizon.

entry.name: Whale Shark
entry.description: Far east of the Philippine islands swims a gentle giant marked with pale spots. Though greater than many ships, this broad-mouthed shark feeds on tiny drifting sea life.

entry.name: Chamorro Slingstone
entry.description: A smooth stone, shaped like a small spindle and sharpened at both ends, is found among relics of the Mariana Islands. Skilled islanders cast such stones from woven slings with remarkable force.

entry.name: Oceanic Manta Ray
entry.description: Across the warm ocean glides a giant ray with wings like dark sails. It sweeps through the blue water with slow strokes, drawing tiny food from the sea.

entry.name: Marine Iguana
entry.description: Upon the black volcanic shores lives a dark lizard that plunges into the surf. Unlike its landbound kin, it grazes on seaweed, then returns to sun-warmed rocks to recover its heat.

entry.name: Orongo Village
entry.description: Above the breakers on a lonely Pacific island lie low stone houses set into a grassy crater rim. Carved rocks recall the ceremonies of a people far from other shores.
